CVE-2026-53669 is a follow-up to CVE-2025-68470 affecting react-router versions 6.0.0 through 6.30.4. The fix requires upgrading to react-router 7.18.0, which is a major version jump from v6 to v7. This major version upgrade carries significant risk of breaking changes and API incompatibilities with the unleash application. The vulnerability has medium severity (CVSS 5.1) and involves scenarios where attacker-supplied paths passed to navigation mechanisms could result in unexpected external navigations. Investigation is ongoing to assess the feasibility of the major version upgrade and whether the vulnerable navigation code paths are exercised in unleash's usage of react-router.

CVE-2026-53666 affects react-router versions 6.4.0 through 6.30.4. The fix requires upgrading to react-router 7.18.0, which is a major version jump from v6 to v7. This major version upgrade carries significant risk of breaking changes and API incompatibilities with the unleash application. The vulnerability has medium severity (CVSS 6.1) and only impacts Framework Mode and Data Mode applications doing manual SSR/hydration, not Declarative Mode. Investigation is ongoing to assess the feasibility of the major version upgrade and whether the vulnerable code paths are exercised in unleash's usage of react-router.

GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 is a CSRF vulnerability in react-router affecting versions 7.12.0 through 8.2.x, fixed in 8.3.0. Upgrading to 8.3.0 requires a major version jump from 7.x to 8.x, which introduces breaking changes and requires significant testing. The opencost-ui application has been updated to 7.18.0, which resolves other high and medium severity vulnerabilities in the 7.x line. The CSRF risk is mitigated by the application's authentication and authorization controls. Monitoring upstream for a backport or evaluating the 8.x upgrade path.
